clue.text: Become entangled with a writer of music

definitions.meaning: threads that ... get knotted and tangled together
Maurice ... was the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: Someone gets romantically mixed up with a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle or snarl threads, and Maurice Ravel was a celebrated French composer.

clue.text: Good grounds to conserve the beer

parts.note: to ration a supply is to conserve it by sharing it out sparingly
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: There is sound reason for saving the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification for something.

clue.text: There are half-a-dozen, every one brought up in a home

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: all means every one

explanation.surface: Six children, all raised in a children's home.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'brought up' reads a word from the bottom upwards; VI is the Roman numeral six.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a country house or detached residence, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Law-breaker discovered as liner cast off

indicators.note: off means the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal revealed when an ocean liner was cast off from its moorings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LINER CAST; 'discovered as' links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A larcenist commits larceny, the crime of theft.

clue.text: Lectured about a point the Frenchwoman cut out

indicators.note: the scolding word goes around the other pieces, so about signals a container here

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or lecture
S, south, is a point of the compass
elle is French for she, the Frenchwoman

explanation.surface: Someone gave a talk on a point that a Frenchwoman deleted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lectured' looks like the definition but is the old past tense of chide; 'about' wraps that scolding word round the compass point and the French pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chiselled has been carved or shaped out with a tool, as a sculptor cuts out a figure.

clue.text: Call to read with discretion

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or read carefully
tact is discretion and delicacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: A phone call should be read with diplomacy.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is an old verb meaning to study, so to read.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone is to get in touch with them, as by telephoning.

clue.text: Repeating it, go on and on about the point

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
to rant is to go on and on about something loudly

explanation.surface: Saying it again, harping on about the main point.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is given as it is; E is east, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterant means repeating, from iterate, to do or say again.

clue.text: Some golden suet pudding to follow

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A golden suet pudding comes next for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'pudding to follow' as the definition, but pudding means nothing like the answer; it belongs to the hiding phrase and 'to follow' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards or result, the sense of coming after.

clue.text: Top man misrepresented about support for putting up gold

indicators.note: the word for misrepresented goes around the other pieces, so about makes a container

parts.note: lied means told untruths, misrepresented things

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting up means the word for support is read upwards

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: The boss gave a false account of backing for a gold investment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'putting up' turns the support word upwards; heraldry uses OR for gold; 'about' sets both inside the word for told untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord is a feudal superior to whom vassals owe allegiance, the man at the top.

clue.text: Making notes on drug store

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on another sits above it, so on orders the pieces

parts.note: D and E are two notes of the musical scale
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone takes notes about a pharmacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug store' reads as a pharmacy; split, D and E (notes) sit on POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storehouse where goods are kept.

clue.text: It's clear Eton developed the liberal spirit

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of the two words have grown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A clear claim that the famous school fostered broad-mindedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges CLEAR and ETON together; Eton is the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the open-minded acceptance of other views, the attitude of a broad-minded liberal.

clue.text: Strips back the nap

indicators.note: back tells us the word for strips is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: peels means strips off, as skin or paint

explanation.surface: Someone strips off at the back before a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PEELS round into SLEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short doze, a brief spell of slumber.

clue.text: Value placed on duck, so to speak

indicators.note: the value word is put after the duck in this across entry, so placed on orders the pieces

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O
to rate is to value or assess

explanation.surface: Putting a price on a duck, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a nought in cricket, giving O; 'placed on' puts RATE after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, to speak pompously at length.

clue.text: A room below ground-level can bring on depression

parts.note: a basement is a storey or room beneath street level

explanation.surface: Living in a cellar flat can make a person feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as low spirits, but the answer means humiliation or lowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is a lowering or humbling, a sinking down in rank or esteem.

clue.text: Pop back, meaning to settle

indicators.note: back makes the word for father run in the opposite direction

parts.note: pop and pa are both informal words for a father
the point of something is its meaning or purpose

explanation.surface: Dad returns, intending to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is an informal word for father, and 'back' turns it round before the word for meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to fix or decide upon, as to settle a time or place for a meeting.

clue.text: Americans always on the level

parts.note: on the level means honest, but here literally living on flat open land such as the prairies

explanation.surface: Praise for American honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the level' means honest; literally, these Americans live on flat grassland such as the Great Plains.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsmen are inhabitants of the Great Plains of North America, flat prairie country.

clue.text: To many in employment this is paramount

indicators.note: the letter for many sits inside the word for a job, so in signals a container

parts.note: a post is a job or position of employment
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, can stand for many

explanation.surface: To most people in work, this matters above all.
explanation.walkthrough: M, the Roman thousand, does duty for 'many'; 'in' puts it inside POST.
explanation.definitionFit: Topmost means highest of all, supreme, which is what paramount means.

clue.text: Beam grabbed by stout painter

indicators.note: the beam word is held inside the stout word, so grabbed by signals a container

parts.note: porter is a dark beer like stout
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A plump artist seized hold of a wooden beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective for the painter but is PORTER, a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayer depicts or represents, as an artist painting a likeness.

clue.text: Dissertations about an alternative, one guesses

indicators.note: the word for dissertations goes around the other pieces, so about makes a container

parts.note: theses are long academic dissertations
or is the word that offers an alternative
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Academic papers on another option, someone supposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' does double duty in the surface reading 'one guesses', but in the parse it is the Roman I and 'guesses' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who theorises forms speculative ideas or suppositions, that is, makes guesses.

clue.text: Resilient, being from Castile

indicators.note: the answer is made from the place name's letters, so being from signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tough and springy because they come from Castile in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being from' rearranges CASTILE, the Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic springs back to shape after stretching, the quality of a resilient material.

clue.text: A woman receiving acclaim in foreign secret service

indicators.note: the agency letters take in the praise word, so receiving signals a container

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, foreign to a British setter
to laud is to praise or acclaim

explanation.surface: A female spy is honoured within an overseas intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency, foreign from a British setter's view; 'receiving' takes the praise word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudia is a female given name.

clue.text: A game contract

parts.note: bridge is a card game, one in which contracts are bid

explanation.surface: A bridge player's bid, the contract in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun from bridge but is the verb, to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten or condense it, making it smaller.

clue.text: A thing?

definitions.meaning: the word a is the indefinite ... in grammar
an item or object, as in an ... of clothing

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' is the indefinite article, and an article is also an object or item.

clue.text: Intimate if don can't make it

indicators.note: make it here means rework the words into something new, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A close friend of a university don who cannot attend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make it' rearranges the letters of IF DON CANT; a don is a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidant is a trusted close friend with whom secrets are shared.

clue.text: Jar in which pounds may be kept in ready money

indicators.note: the pounds symbol is held inside the money word, so kept in signals a container

parts.note: cash is ready money, notes and coins
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A pot in which one keeps pounds of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' looks like a container noun but is a verb, to grate or conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash is to conflict or jar, as clashing colours or sounds grate.

clue.text: Big business abandons the effort to provide running water

indicators.note: abandons means the effort word is dropped from the business word

parts.note: industry is large-scale manufacturing and commerce
a try is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: A large firm gives up trying to supply mains water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' takes TRY out of INDUSTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan, a flowing body of fresh water.

clue.text: A revolting individual put to flight

definitions.meaning: someone who rises up against authority is a rebel in revolt
the upright board in each step of a staircase is put into a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A rebel was chased off and fled.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is one who rises in revolt, and also the vertical part of each stair in a flight.

clue.text: Curbs straggling bushes

indicators.note: straggling suggests the letters have wandered out of line and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Hedges that keep growing out of bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straggling' rearranges CURBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrub is land covered with stunted shrubs and brushwood.

clue.text: Prepared for conflict with certain members

definitions.meaning: having limbs, that is arms, as body parts

explanation.surface: Ready for battle alongside some fellow members.
explanation.definitionFit: To be armed is to carry weapons, and also, literally, to possess upper limbs.

clue.text: Where the monitors used to be put right

definitions.text: Where the monitors used to be put right

parts.words: Where the monitors used to be put right
parts.note: monitors were shallow-draught warships, and the places they were repaired were naval yards

explanation.surface: Where screens or class prefects were once corrected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monitors' suggests screens or school prefects; here they are a class of old warships, mended in naval repair yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dockyards are shipyards where naval vessels such as monitors were built and repaired.

clue.text: Workers given fish as a gesture of goodwill

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as on a farm or ship
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Labourers receive fish as a friendly present.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another person's palm is a friendly greeting or sign of agreement.

clue.text: Military personnel with transport problem

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a bus is a vehicle of public transport

explanation.surface: Soldiers have trouble with their vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words, a kind of brain-teaser.
